newsitem.title: UK: Potential Asia bank privatisations seen at $250bln.
newsitem.headline: Potential Asia bank privatisations seen at $250bln.

text.p: Moves by Asian governments to reduce their involvement in their banking sectors could lead to $250 billion worth of privatisations, according to research by Robert Fleming & Co.

In its monthly emerging markets focus, Flemings said that Asian governments now saw a chance to rid themselves of possible burdens or cash in on their investments thanks to the high profitability of banks over the past five years.

"Assuming a reasonable level of valuation (where market value equals 12 percent of assets) for these nationalised banks, we find that there are currently $250 billion in potential privatisations out there," analyst Vinod Changarath said.
The amount would be equivalent to 19 percent of the market capitalisation of the countries involved.
Regardless of their reasons for getting into banking, governments were now trying to get out, he said.

"This is because privatisation is the buzzword of the 1990s, their banks are unprofitable, the managements are bureaucratic and resistant to change, and government-owned banks have tended to run into asset quality problems."
The report said Indonesia, India and Malaysia represented the leading markets for bank privatisation, with an aggregate $23 billion potentially up for offer in these countries.
China and Taiwan have enormous potential but privatisation is likely to be slowed by the absence of fundamental state-owned enterprise reform in China, and vested political interests in Taiwan.
Sri Lanka and Pakistan may come to the market in the longer term.

Changarath said Indonesia was on track for a significant privatisation programme with one of seven state-owned banks, BNI, partly privatised in 1996 and two more strong candidates, Bank Ekspor and Bank Tabungan Negara, waiting in the wings.
In Malaysia a public offering of shares is expected to be made soon in the country's second largest bank, Bank Bumiputra, and the government holds over 50 percent in the largest, Malayan Banking.

A number of public share offerings are in the pipeline in India, including Dena Bank, Bank of Baroda, Bank of India, Canara Bank and Corporation Bank. The state currently controls 72 percent of the total banking assets of the country.
